pcs.pc_description: Wear the appropriate PPE and clothing designed for handling LMO while checking the vehicle
Ensure that there are no flammable items, greasy rags or diesel in the vehicle
Ensure the used tools are cleaned for oxygen service, and the toolkit is stowed in a place away from the cargo
Ensure the vehicle is fitted with GPS tracking and cooperate with monitoring requirements.
Conduct regular inspections of essential vehicle systems (e.g., brakes, tyres, fluid levels, electrical systems) to ensure they are in optimal working condition before operating the vehicle.

Follow the manufacturer’s maintenance schedule for servicing key components like the engine, transmission, brakes, and exhaust system. Ensure all service activities are conducted in a timely manner to prevent wear and potential failure.
Check and replace parts that have a limited lifespan, such as air filters, fuel filters, wiper blades, and spark plugs, ensuring they meet operational standards.

Inspect tyre pressure, tread depth, and overall tyre condition. Perform tyre rotations or replacements as necessary and ensure the correct tyre specifications are used for optimal vehicle performance.
Regularly check and maintain all critical fluid levels (e.g., engine oil, brake fluid, coolant, power steering fluid) to prevent engine overheating, brake failure, or other system malfunctions.
Inspect the braking system to ensure it is functioning properly, checking brake pads, discs, and fluid levels. Replace worn components as part of routine maintenance.
Test and maintain the vehicle’s electrical systems, including battery charge, alternator performance, and wiring, to prevent electrical failures during operation.
Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the vehicle for signs of wear and tear, such as leaks, cracks, or damaged parts, and address issues before they become critical.

Regularly check that the vehicle’s maintenance tools (e.g., jack, wrench, tyre repair kit) are in working condition and stored properly. Clean and maintain tools as needed to ensure they are ready for use.
Identify and report any signs of potential mechanical issues, such as unusual sounds, vibrations, or system failures, during preventive maintenance checks.
Keep accurate records of all preventive maintenance activities performed on the vehicle, including dates, parts replaced, and any issues identified, for reference and future inspections.

• • Check that the vehicle meets basic legal and compliance requirements: • •The organization guidelines, e.g. rule books • •CMVR guidelines from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway and other guidelines issued by Road Transport Authorities like RTOs • •PESO, and medical oxygen-specific transport guidelines • •Any other safety, security and environmental guidelines • •WHO & MoHFW Oxygen Transport Guidelines (esp. post-COVID)
Ensure that the valid documents are available in the vehicle (License, fitness certification, insurance, copy of registration certificate and road tax paid)
Check vehicle service records indicative of any history of technical defects
Check the safety devices in the vehicle, such as wheel chocks, breakdown signs, spark arrestors, traffic cone and fire extinguisher
Ensure that DCP fire extinguishers are available in the vehicle and have valid 3rd party certification of condition
Check the cooling system, steering, electrical, fluid levels, braking system and other general conditions of the vehicle
Ensure that there are no leakages in the cooling system
Perform the free play test to check the steering
Examine the fluid levels – oil levels, engine oil, gearbox hydraulic oil, brakes fluid, washer liquid and fuel
Check the braking systems to ensure it is working properly
Perform the start-stop test to check the electrical system of the vehicle.
Always stay on the planned route as approved by the transporter
Report actual or possible defects to the senior driver, owner, or service supervisor in detail so that they can diagnose the problem
In consultation with the owner, conclude about the roadworthiness of the vehicle and, if found unfit, decide to use another vehicle.

pcs.pc_description: Follow the standard driving practices while driving LMO tankers
Follow the working/driving hours assigned; in case of emergency, comply with instructions regarding extended hours.
Follow prescribed work and rest schedules to manage fatigue and ensure safe driving
Operate the vehicle with a co-driver when assigned during emergency situations.
Follow the safety precautions while loading liquid oxygen to the tankers
Maintain a speed limit of 10 km/hr within the factory premises before loading oxygen
Check the availability of cones, signs, PPE, emergency kit, etc.
Check the decanting and venting procedures before driving
Follow the safety precautions while parking LMO tankers
Park the vehicle only on open ground with sufficient air circulation; do not park under high- tension cables (11kV).
Check the pressure gauge once every 4 hours
Follow the safety precautions while unloading the liquid oxygen and exiting the delivery site
Maintain a speed limit of 5 Km/hr while driving at the delivery site
Follow the safety precautions during the empty return of tankers
Ensure that TREM (Transport Emergency) Card and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) are carried at all times and adhered to.
Ensure the availability of Emergency Number and Valid Chief Controller of Explosives (CCoE) Peso Certificate
Follow the assigned geo-fenced route without deviation; if the vehicle enters unspecified zones or misses the route, alerts will be raised.
Enter city limits only after 11 PM and exit before 4 AM, or as per the traffic regulations of the respective city.
Follow Eco-Driving Practices and Emission Compliance to Encourage fuel-saving and low- emission
Apply various defensive driving techniques while overtaking, parking, stopping, driving in the rain, driving at night, etc., while maneuvering through turns and curves.
Practice the mechanism of managing cargo pressure on the road while driving on curvy roads, braking hazards, etc.
Use safe driving principles to assess risks and make prompt, situation-based decisions.
Follow necessary precautions and road signs to avoid roll over, braking hazards and possible accidents
Always remain alert while driving and handle stress effectively
Limit stoppages as per prescribed norms and justify any additional stoppages.
Follow state-specific traffic regulations, including lane discipline, and adhere to lawful procedures while changing lanes or turning.

Maintain a safe following distance from other vehicles and clearly signal your intentions using appropriate indicators. Respond appropriately to permanent and temporary traffic signals, road signs, markings, and hand signals from traffic personnel, using a safe and systematic driving routine.
Use indicators and parking lights when stationary; Choose a safe, legal, and convenient location for stopping the vehicle when required.
Secure the vehicle safely on gradients using hand brakes and wheel chocks; check for approaching cyclists, pedestrians, and other vehicles before opening the door
Remain calm and composed in challenging situations such as traffic congestion or accidents. Avoid confrontations or disputes with other road users and members of the public.
Give priority and right of way to children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their safety and comfort on the road.
Observe movement of pedestrians and stray animals to avoid collision
Comply with relevant rules and best practices when dealing with the general public, and demonstrate awareness and compassion toward stray animals on the road.

pcs.pc_description: Wear appropriate clothing and PPE ( face and head shield, full sleeves, covered clothing, covered shoes, 100% cotton or wool, cryogenic gloves) while handling liquid oxygen
Ensure that PPE is worn at all times and any clothing coming in contact with liquid oxygen must be removed immediately
Ensure that there is no smoking, cooking or open flames in any area where liquid oxygen is stored or handled
Ensure that no liquid oxygen or oxygen- enriched air comes in contact with flammable or combustible substances of any kind
Use only oxygen-compatible materials and lubricants
Check that the Cryogenic containers are always in an upright position while being transported, handled or stored
Ensure that the cryogenic containers are not tipped, slided or rolled on their side while moving
Use a suitable hand truck or trolley for moving small containers
Avoid mechanical and thermal shock while moving cryogenic oxygen cylinders
Use only transfer lines and equipment designed for use with cryogenic liquids and ensure that they are well insulated
Ensure that the appropriate protocol is followed while loading of oxygen into tank
Inspect that a diffuser is attached to the transfer hose to reduce turbulence & release of gas while filling up from tanker
Review the decantation and venting procedure for the tank
Monitor the pressure gauge as per the prescribed guidelines and always wear a PPE
Follow the appropriate procedure for rupture disk and valve failure
Follow the emergency protocol for leaks, spills, rupture disk and valve failure
Follow all the statutory requirements of the chief controller of Explosives in India, SMPV rules and follow MSDS guidelines at all times during handling and transportation

GS2. Communicate clearly and concisely during stressful situations with authorities and team members.
GS3. Maintain composure and make logical decisions under pressure.
GS4. Record emergency details clearly in written format or through electronic means.
GS5. Follow instructions from control centers or emergency responders.

pcs.pc_description: Identify early signs of potential emergency situations such as hissing/unusual sounds, gas odour (oxygen leaks), pressure gauge fluctuations, or alerts from vehicle safety systems.
Monitor safety indicators in the vehicle (e.g., temperature, pressure) and react promptly to abnormalities.
Shut off valves only if it is safe for the driver to do so and isolate the LMO container if there's a suspected or visible leak.
Use safety equipment like spill kits or oxygen masks as per protocol.
Report any malfunction or wear and tear in LMO-specific components (e.g., pressure systems, valves, temperature control) to prevent breakdowns or leakage.
Identify fire risk from LMO vapor in oxygen- enriched environments.
Check whether it is safe to disconnect power sources.
Once confirmed, disconnect all power sources according to standard safety procedures.
Operate the battery cut-off switch immediately in case of emergency to eliminate any ignition source
Use appropriate firefighting equipment or sand to control minor fires, ensuring personal safety first.
Avoid use of water or incorrect extinguishing methods for LMO-related fires.
Call fire services immediately and provide details about LMO cargo.
Park the vehicle in an isolated location, preferably against the wind, during emergencies to reduce risk of fire or exposure.
Evacuate the area and instruct others to maintain a safe distance (as per HAZMAT safety norms).
Administer first aid to self or others in case of minor injuries or health incidents (if trained).
Ensure that proper first aid kits for cold burns are available in the vehicle
Implement safety protocols for medical emergencies involving self or others (e.g., symptoms of hypoxia, heatstroke, or panic attacks), and administer first aid where appropriate.
Activate emergency brakes and switch off the ignition safely if required; activate vehicle hazard indicators and place safety cones, reflective triangles, or barricades to warn other road users.
Inform authorities and follow vehicle breakdown protocols.
Coordinate with alternate transport or towing services.
Ensure bystanders and the public remain at a safe distance from the breakdown site by using cones, hazard lights, or warning signs
Turn on hazard lights and place warning triangles or cones to alert other road users.
Evacuate the area and instruct others to maintain a safe distance (as per HAZMAT safety norms).
Move the vehicle to a safe zone, if possible and safe to do so, to prevent escalation.
Secure the cargo area to prevent movement or spillage of LMO tanks during an emergency stop or accident.
Inform the control center, nearby emergency response teams, and local authorities (fire, police) immediately in case of a serious incident. Immediately contact the assigned company emergency SPOC
Cooperate fully with responding authorities and emergency personnel.
Maintain continuous communication with the company emergency coordination center throughout the incident to receive guidance and updates.
Carry and maintain an updated contact list of police, fire department, and emergency services for all locations along the route.
Conduct pre-trip safety and emergency equipment checks to minimize risk of in-transit incidents.
Participate in regular emergency response drills and simulations conducted by the employer or regulatory bodies.
Ensure emergency equipment (first aid kit, fire extinguisher, PPE, etc.) is regularly inspected and in working condition.
Follow all safety and compliance procedures as laid out in LMO transport SOPs.
Ensure proper documentation of the incident, including time, location, nature of emergency, actions taken, persons involved, and reporting details.
Refer to and follow instructions provided in TREM (Transport Emergency) Card and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) during emergencies.

modules.module_title: Follow health, safety and security procedures

pcs.pc_description: Make note of all safety processes in different location (cargo loading area, ramp operation area, etc.) with reference to area of operation.
Wear all PPE such as goggles, ear plugs, helmet, mask, shoes, etc. as applicable in the cargo movement area.
Follow standard driving practice to ensure safety of life and material.
Follow organizational protocol to deploy action in case of signs of any emergency situation or accident or breach of safety.
Undertake periodical preventive health check ups and stay physically fit for driving attentively.
Undertake fitness test including mandatory certified eye test once every 6 months.
Take appropriate breaks, have adequate sleep, drink water etc and perform stretch exercises when required.
Follow security procedures like green gate in port, customs area, factory security, etc.
Comply with data safety regulations of the organisation.
Follow standard safety procedures and precautions while handling hazardous / fragile cargo.

modules.module_title: Ensure compliance to safety and security

pcs.pc_description: Recognise unsafe conditions and safety practices at the loading area and report it to concerned authority.
Inspect the activity area and equipment for appropriate, safe condition.
Always follow road safety and traffic rules.
Never drink alcohol before or during your trip and avoid taking medication without doctor consultation during driving.
Undergo alcohol check-up before every trip and ensure zero alcohol consumption.
Comply with Alcohol Detector Sensor (ADS) readings installed in the vehicle
Check if extinguishers and safety gear are available in the vehicle and in working condition.
Participate in fire drills of the organization.
Ensure that standard material handling procedure are being followed while loading.
Check if all the safety and security related tags, labels and signage are placed in the cargo.
Confirm if loading instrument is certified and operational.
Implement 5S at workplace.
Check if cargo has passed security checks and report in case of any violation.

In case of accident/ collision, check whether everyone involved are fine, and treat for medical injuries as needed and to the level of your training and inform to authorities/ medical team and follow SOP.
